data.description:
# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`
in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) invalidates a stored audit when any
fingerprint component changes. The original formulation fingerprinted
**whole-repo** state (git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files +
whole-repo working-tree hash), so any commit or uncommitted/untracked change
anywhere in the repository — even one from an *unrelated* work item — invalidated
every stored audit and re-triggered the full audit pipeline.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD
`310773d5`; afterwards an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged
`aaabdede` to dev, the fingerprint changed (`58947e06…` matched recomputation at
`310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), the re-audit ran and blocked on the pre-flight
full-suite cache gate — a verified item stuck in review.

**Current state (2026-10-21, HEAD `fe85415a3`):** the whole-repo components have
**already been replaced** by per-touched-file scoping (SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, done):
the payload is now `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` where each
touched path contributes its committed state (blob hash at HEAD, else the latest
touching commit) plus its narrowed working-tree state. An unrelated commit or
working-tree change now invalidates **only if it touches a file in the item's
touched set** (commits referencing the item id + comment-recorded commit hashes +
Key Files). The whole-repo HEAD sha is no longer a component, and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` no longer exists. The observed failure case is
therefore **no longer reproducible** with today's formula.

The remaining delta of this item is the **strict rule** recorded in the original
Q&A: "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data
AFTER the audit was created." That rule is stronger than the current
per-touched-file formula — it requires a fingerprint over the item's own data
only (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git
calls**, so even a committed/uncommitted change to a file this item touched does
not invalidate.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness
  short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid
unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity
(including changes to files this item happened to touch) doesn't invalidate my
audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data
   only** — the item's title + description (the description contains the ACs and
   the Key Files section, so `key_files` may remain in the payload as a
   deterministic derivative of it). The per-path git components (committed HEAD
   blob hashes, working-tree state) and the whole-repo HEAD component are

## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.
2. A regression test asserts ruff is never invoked with a `.yaml`/`.yml` file path when the changed-file list includes one, and that no finding work items are created for non-Python files.
3. Directory-scan behavior (`files=None`) is unchanged.
4. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected (existing tests pass).

## Summary

The audit runner's code-quality scan is documented to lint only the work item's changed files (`SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1: "the code-quality scan runs only over the git changed-file list … not the full repo"), but it silently falls back to a **whole-repo** scan whenever the changed-file list is empty. For an item whose work is already committed to `dev` (the normal post-merge state, and the state the merge gate integrates to), `git diff --name-only HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` are both empty, so `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files or None)` receives `None` and lints the entire repository. Any pre-existing critical/high ruff finding in an unrelated file then blocks Phase 1 of every audit in that repo — a recurrence of the defect class fixed by `SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P` ("EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files") and a contradiction of `SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1.

## Repro

1. Work item `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (llm) is merged to `origin/dev`; the local checkout is clean at the delivered commit `66ddbe93`.
2. `git diff --name-only HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are both empty.
3. Run `audit_runner.py issue LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS --force`: `_git_changed_files` returns `[]`, so `run_code_quality(files=None)` scans the whole repo.
4. The whole-repo scan returns 4 findings, all outside the item's change set:
   - `ruff F841` (critical) `proxy/tests/test_watchdog_upstream_cancellation.py:197,277`
   - `ruff I001` (medium) `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py:594`, `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py:503`
5. Phase 1 blocks on the critical findings; every AC is demoted `met → partial` and Phase 2 is skipped; `Ready to close: No`.

Verified directly: `run_code_quality(project_root=<llm>, files=[the item's 4 changed files])` returns **0 findings** — the item's own work is lint-clean.

## Impact (observed)

- The audit of `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (2026-09-26) produced a spurious `Ready to close: No` from findings belonging to other work items. The item was only accepted because the Phase 1 false-positive screen *also* degraded (provider error / concurrency limit), leaving the run fallback-tainted and the lifecycle restored to `completed`/`in_review`.
- Had the screen succeeded, the `F841` findings would have been classified `genuine` and the unrelated item would have been **demoted** `in_review → open`.
- The findings already have tracking items (quality epics): `LP-0MUHSWSI8004AFU4`, `LP-0MUHSWS8M001QY46`, `LP-0MUHVMLGB0056C0K`.

## Suggested fix

- When the git changed-file list is empty, scope the code-quality scan to the item's **Key Files** and/or its committed diff (the commits the merge gate resolved, e.g. `git diff-tree -r --name-only <commit>^..<commit>`), instead of falling back to the whole repo.
- An empty effective scope should lint nothing (skip with a documented reason), never the entire repository.
- Cover the already-merged / clean-checkout case in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py`.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_git_changed_files`, `_resolve_touched_files`, and both `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files or None)` call sites (Phase 1 scan ~L11011, remediation re-scan ~L10818)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — Phase 1 code-quality scan call-argument tests (scope resolution)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_remediation.py` — remediation re-scan tests (second call site)
- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `_run_ruff_check` treats a falsy `files` list as a whole-project scan, so an empty scope must skip the call rather than pass `[]`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — the code-quality scoping contract this bug contradicts

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For an item whose work is already committed and whose checkout is clean, the audit code-quality scan lints only the item's files (Key Files and/or its delivered commits), never the whole repo.
2. An empty effective scope lints nothing: the scan is skipped with a documented reason surfaced through the existing `cq_skipped_reason` (rendered as `code_quality_skipped_reason`), rather than scanning the whole repository. Passing `files=[]` is not sufficient — `_run_ruff_check` treats a falsy list as a whole-project scan.

# Verify item-data-only audit freshness contract

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an audit operator, I want independent, executable proof that a stored audit is invalidated *only* by a change to this work item's own audited data (title/description/ACs/Key Files), so that unrelated repository activity can never silently invalidate or (worse) mask a stale audit.

**Why a separate verification item:** the parent's AC8 requires that no existing coverage is silently dropped. This item owns that guarantee: it enumerates the old per-touched-path / comment-contribution contract, proves each case is now asserted the *new* way, and adds mutation-style guards that fail if any git- or comment-derived component is ever reintroduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Non-invalidation regression tests assert the fingerprint is **unchanged** across all three previously-invalidating conditions: (a) HEAD movement caused by another work item's commit, (b) uncommitted/untracked working-tree changes anywhere in the repo, (c) committed, staged or dirty changes **to a file this item itself touched** (the direct reversal of `test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change` / `..._dirty` / `..._staged` and `test_tool_artefact_rewrite_invalidates`).
2. Invalidation regression tests assert the fingerprint **changes** when the item's title changes, when its description/ACs change, and when its `Key Files` section changes.
3. Non-invalidation tests assert the fingerprint is unchanged after: adding a comment (including a comment recording a commit hash), and changing `status` / `stage` / `priority` / `assignee` / `sortIndex` (all of which move `updatedAt`).
4. A mutation-style guard asserts `_compute_content_fingerprint` makes **zero** git calls: with the runner's git-executing helpers patched to raise, a fingerprint is still returned; and an exact-payload test asserts the hashed payload keys are exactly the item-data schema (no `path_states`, no `head`/`worktree`, no comment-derived keys), so reintroducing a component fails a test.
5. Versioned-line tests: the persisted report's `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hex>` line round-trips through `_extract_content_fingerprint`; an unversioned legacy line (`Audit content fingerprint: <hex>`) makes `_extract_content_fingerprint` return `None` and the gate falls back to the time floor (fresh inside `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS` + persist-write tolerance, stale beyond it); `check-freshness --json` reports `hasFingerprint: false` for a legacy v1 report and `true` for a v2 report.
6. Child-reuse coverage: `_get_child_audit_verdict` / `_child_content_changed` reuse a child whose own data is unchanged, and treat a title/description change as stale.
7. A ledger comment on this item lists **every** pre-existing freshness test that was rewritten, kept or removed, with the reason for each — so nothing is silently dropped (parent AC8).

`git worktree add` and any checkout/merge in the SorraAgents repo exit 127 because the committed `post-checkout` / `post-merge` / `post-rewrite` hooks (`skill/.githooks/`) unconditionally `exec` `/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, which does not exist on this host. This breaks `wl sync` (its temporary-worktree merge) and will break `implement.py start`/`finish` (worktree creation) for SA items. ContentCreator's copies of the same hooks were updated to be self-contained (inline `wl sync --git-branch refs/worklog/data` with `WORKLOG_SKIP_*` bypass); SorraAgents's were not.

## Reproduction

```
cd /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-test HEAD
# → /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: ...: not found
# → rc=127
```

Workaround that does not mutate repo config:
`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/dev/null wl sync --worklog-dir .worklog`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git worktree add` succeeds (rc 0) in a fresh SorraAgents worktree; post-checkout does not fail when the central script path is absent.
- [ ] `wl sync` from the SorraAgents root succeeds without the env-var workaround.
- [ ] The updated hooks keep ContentCreator behaviour (self-contained `wl sync --git-branch refs/worklog/data` with `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_CHECKOUT=1`/`WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` bypasses) and remain committed in this repo.
- [ ] All related documentation updated (hooks README / docs/dev/worklog-sync.md if it mentions the delegated path).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Related work

- Discovered while running intake for `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (implement.py finish status store) — its sync step hit this.
- Related: `docs/dev/worklog-sync-identity.md` mentions `config.defaults.yaml` author gating used by the newer hooks.

## Summary

`wl sync` is blocked **again**, for a new reason: two commits pushed to
`refs/worklog/data` *after* the last synced tip are authored by the incident
sentinel identity `t@t.com`, which the project deliberately refuses (the
quarantine from SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC AC4 — `t@t.com` must never be added to
`syncAllowedAuthors`).

Observed 2026-10-22 (this session):

```
$ wl sync --dry-run --json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Refusing to merge worklog data from refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 2 incoming commit(s) fail the author-identity gate.
- 2a52d4b0c: author email 't@t.com' does not match configured user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'
- eab767421: author email 't@t.com' does not match configured user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'"
}
```

## Evidence

- Local `last-synced-ref` = `3276d1a58` (past the 4 original `pi@local`
  offenders — the SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS remediation worked).
- Remote ref scan window `3276d1a58..refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`:
  3 commits — `8198300cf` (correct GitHub identity, 22:33) plus
  `eab767421` (22:47) and `2a52d4b0c` (22:49), both authored `t@t.com`.
- Both `t@t.com` commits are ordinary **delta** snapshots
  (`{"__worklog_sync__":{"kind":"delta","version":1}}`) carrying real
  worklog content (e.g. item `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` and its comments) — the
  data itself is legitimate; only the commit identity is wrong.
- Every checkout/worktree on this host reports the correct identity
  (`git config user.email` = `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`,
  verified for the main checkout and all 25 linked worktrees), so the pushes
  came from an environment with a stale/default `t@t.com` identity (another
  machine, container, or a checkout that overrode `user.email`).
- `wl sync` refuses, so local worklog mutations cannot be pushed; the
  pre-push hook fails open (`worklog: pre-push sync failed (pushing anyway)`),
  so code pushes to `dev` still work.

## Why this is durable-harm, not just a one-off

A fresh clone has no `last-synced-ref`, so the gate scans the whole remote ref
history. `t@t.com` is forbidden in the allow-list, so every fresh clone will
refuse to sync until those commits are either re-authored/purged from
`refs/worklog/data` or the project quarantine decision is revisited.

## Remediation options (operator decision required)

- **(a) One-time `wl sync --allow-foreign-author`** — the same escape hatch
  used for the `pi@local` incident. Merges the two deltas, and the next
  correctly-authored push advances `last-synced-ref` past them. Does not fix
  fresh clones (they still scan full history and refuse), and merges
  sentinel-authored commits without quarantine.
- **(b) Re-author the two commits on `refs/worklog/data`** (re-parent with the
  correct identity, trees unchanged) and force-push the worklog ref. Durable
  for fresh clones; a shared-ref force-push (precedented by the
  SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC purge) and therefore operator-authorized work only.
- **(c) Find and fix the producer first** — identify the checkout/environment
  pushing as `t@t.com`, repair its `user.email`, then apply (a) or (b).
  Without (c) the same commits will be regenerated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `wl sync` (no flags) completes with no author-identity refusal; `last-synced-ref` advances past `2a52d4b0c`.
- [ ] **AC2** The chosen remediation is operator-authorized and recorded in a comment with the exact command(s) and output.
- [ ] **AC3** `t@t.com` remains absent from `syncAllowedAuthors` (the sentinel quarantine is preserved) and `scripts/check_git_identity.py` still flags it.
- [ ] **AC4** The source of the `t@t.com`-authored sync commits is identified (or explicitly accepted as unknown), so recurrence is understood.
- [ ] **AC5** No worklog data is lost: the imported deltas' items (e.g. `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6`) are present locally and in the pushed remote ref.

## Key Files

- `.worklog/last-synced-ref`, `.worklog/config.yaml` (read-only verification)
- `refs/worklog/data` / `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data` (git refs)
